summary: beautifyText ships an import-time and install-time C2 beacon with remote shell and file read/write
details: beautifyText 1.0.3 is a backdoor disguised as a text utility. On `import beautifyText`, the package spawns a detached background Python process (via a module named `_compat`) that decodes a base64-obfuscated C2 URL (https://bleodw.wisp.uno) and enters a long-poll loop against `/work/{id}`. The command channel implements three job kinds: `exec` runs arbitrary shell commands via subprocess with `shell=True`, `pull` reads arbitrary files from the installer's host, and `push` writes arbitrary files to the installer's host, with results POSTed back to `/result`. On registration, host metadata (hostname, OS/release, Python version, USER/USERNAME, current working directory) is sent to `/register`, and `/heartbeat` maintains the session. setup.py installs an `install` and `develop` cmdclass override whose `run()` calls `_post_install()`, which imports `beautifyText._compat` and triggers the same beacon during `pip install`, so the backdoor activates on install even without a subsequent import. The C2 host is stored as a base64 literal (`_HOST_B64 = aHR0cHM6Ly9ibGVvZHcud2lzcC51bm8=`) and decoded at runtime to evade static string matching. The process is detached so it survives parent-process exit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
